entities.summary: Jean Ribault was a French naval officer, navigator, and a colonizer of what would become the southeastern United States. He was a major figure in the French attempts to colonize Florida. A Huguenot and officer under Admiral Gaspard de Coligny, Ribault led an expedition to the New World in 1562 that founded the outpost of Charlesfort on Parris Island in present-day South Carolina. Two years later, he took over command of the French colony of Fort Caroline in what is now Jacksonville, Florida. historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ribault's expedition to the New World in 1562 and his establishment of Fort Caroline had significant regional impact on the colonization of Florida. His death at the hands of Spanish soldiers led to the eventual French abandonment of their colonies in North America.
